market_question: SCOTUS accepts sports event contract case by July 31, 2026?
reasoning: The Supreme Court grants cert in only about 1% of petitions, and a case explicitly targeting sports event contracts as regulated derivatives is extremely niche. There is no well-known pending circuit split or cert petition on this issue, and the 18-month window leaves little time for new litigation to mature through lower courts and receive a grant. While a surprise enforcement action by the CFTC could theoretically produce a fast‑tracked petition, the overall likelihood remains well below the market's 13.5% implied probability.
evidence_points: SCOTUS grants cert in ~1% of petitions annually, making any specific case unlikely to be selected.
No prominent federal appellate case currently addressing sports event contracts as derivatives under the Commodity Exchange Act.
Even if a new enforcement action began now, the full litigation and cert petition process would stretch beyond July 2026 in most scenarios.
sources_consulted: General observation of SCOTUS cert grant rates
News on CFTC v. Kalshi (election contracts, not sports)
West Flagler v. Haaland (tribal gaming compact, not derivatives)
